body.statement: Under effective \(K\)-valued inputs, \(\operatorname{Cert}_{uv,m,G}(B,Q)\) terminates and is sound and complete. It returns incompatibility exactly when \(\mathcal S(B,Q;G)=\varnothing\); conditional on \(\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\ne\varnothing\), it returns one rational function exactly when \(\mathcal H_{uv}(B,Q;G)\) consists of one rational function; otherwise it returns two attained stable pairs \((A,D),(A',D')\in\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\) satisfying \((A_{vu}-A'_{vu})^2+(A_{vu}A'_{vv}-A'_{vu}A_{vv})^2>0\). The certificate remains complete for zero diagonals, zero queried edges, open fibers, positive-dimensional fibers, and branch mergers.
body.justification: A total formula-or-ambiguity output replaces numerical root selection by an auditable causal identification certificate.
body.gap: Classical CAD decides semialgebraic formulas and classical root methods select branches; neither provides this target-aware graph-recursive contract with covariance filtering and exact transfer-distinct witnesses.
body.consumer: Software for subsampled process-DAG analysis can refuse false singleton answers and furnish two explicit observationally equivalent causal explanations when identification fails.
body.proof_tex:
Fix the effective \(K\)-valued matrices \(B,Q\), the supplied graph \(G\), and the known integer \(m\geq 2\).  Define the index set
\[
 \mathcal I_G
 =\{(i,i):i\in V\}\cup
   \{(i,j):j<i\text{ and }j\to i\text{ in }G\}.
\]
For every \((i,j)\in\mathcal I_G\), introduce a real variable \(a_{ij}\), and introduce real variables \(d_1,\ldots,d_d\).  Let \(\widetilde A(a)\) have entry \(a_{ij}\) on \(\mathcal I_G\) and zero elsewhere, and let \(\widetilde D(d)=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_d)\).  Thus the lower-triangular and graph-support restrictions in \(\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\) are imposed by the coordinate parametrization itself.

Consider the finite system
\[
 \bigl[\widetilde A(a)^m\bigr]_{ij}=B_{ij}
 \quad(i,j\in V),                                                   \tag{1}
\]
\[
 \left[\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}\widetilde A(a)^r\widetilde D(d)
                    \bigl(\widetilde A(a)^r\bigr)^\top\right]_{ij}
 =Q_{ij}
 \quad(i,j\in V),                                                   \tag{2}
\]
and
\[
 -1<a_{ii}<1\quad(i\in V),
 \qquad d_i>0\quad(i\in V).                                        \tag{3}
\]
Every left-hand side in (1)--(2) is a polynomial in finitely many variables with coefficients in \(K\), by \(\mathrm{ass{:}effective\mbox{-}input}\).  Since \(\widetilde A(a)\) is triangular,
\[
 \det\!\bigl(\lambda I-\widetilde A(a)\bigr)
   =\prod_{i=1}^d(\lambda-a_{ii}),
 \qquad
 \rho\!\bigl(\widetilde A(a)\bigr)=\max_i|a_{ii}|.
\]
Consequently the first collection of strict inequalities in (3) is equivalent to stability.  Moreover, for every nonzero \(x\in\mathbb R^d\),
\[
 x^\top\widetilde D(d)x=\sum_{i=1}^d d_i x_i^2>0
\]
if and only if every \(d_i>0\).  Hence the second collection in (3) is equivalent to \(\widetilde D(d)\succ0\).  It follows from \(\mathrm{def{:}compatible\mbox{-}fiber}\) that
\[
 (a,d)\longmapsto\bigl(\widetilde A(a),\widetilde D(d)\bigr)         \tag{4}
\]
is a bijection from the realization of (1)--(3) onto \(\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\).  In particular, this encoding neither adds boundary points nor replaces strict positivity or strict stability by their closures.

For a triangular matrix, the diagonal part of (1) is
\[
 a_{ii}^{\,m}=B_{ii},\qquad i\in V.                                 \tag{5}
\]
The effective arithmetic, sign tests, and real-root isolation supplied by the definition of \(K\) enumerate the real roots of each equation (5) and decide the strict inequalities in (3).  There is exactly one real root of \(x^m=b\) when \(m\) is odd; when \(m\) is even there are zero, one, or two real roots according as \(b<0\), \(b=0\), or \(b>0\).  Thus there are finitely many surviving diagonal branches, all represented exactly in \(K\).  If none survives, (4) shows that the compatible fiber is empty.

Fix one surviving branch and process off-diagonal pairs \((v,u)\) in increasing order of \(v-u\), as prescribed by \(\mathrm{def{:}graph\mbox{-}recursion}\).  The lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}path\mbox{-}expansion}\) gives
\[
 a_{vu}C_m(a_{vv},a_{uu})
   =B_{vu}-R_{vu,m}\!\bigl(\widetilde A(a)\bigr).                  \tag{6}
\]
Every off-diagonal coordinate occurring on the right-hand side of (6) has smaller endpoint gap.  The diagonal entries in
\[
 c_{vu}:=C_m(a_{vv},a_{uu})                                        \tag{7}
\]
are fixed on the branch, so \(c_{vu}\in K\).  The lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}divided\mbox{-}difference\mbox{-}zero\mbox{-}set}\), together with the exact sign tests in \(K\), decides whether \(c_{vu}=0\).  In particular, the odd-factor case \(a_{vv}=a_{uu}=0\) and the even-factor case \(a_{vv}=-a_{uu}\) are retained as singular cases.

If \(u\to v\) is graph-allowed and \(c_{vu}\neq0\), equation (6) is equivalent to the unique substitution
\[
 a_{vu}
 =\frac{B_{vu}-R_{vu,m}\!\bigl(\widetilde A(a)\bigr)}{c_{vu}}.     \tag{8}
\]
This is the only division in the recursion, and it is made only after the nonzero test.  Because \(c_{vu}^{-1}\in K\) is a fixed coefficient on the branch, and because all previously eliminated coordinates are polynomials over \(K\) in the coordinates retained so far, substitution of (8) into later transition and covariance equations again produces polynomials over \(K\) in the residual variables; it introduces no variable denominator.  If \(c_{vu}=0\), the coordinate is not eliminated and the induced equation
\[
 B_{vu}-R_{vu,m}\!\bigl(\widetilde A(a)\bigr)=0                    \tag{9}
\]
is retained.  If the edge is forbidden, \(a_{vu}=0\) by the support parametrization and the transition equation (9) is likewise retained, regardless of the value of \(c_{vu}\).

Induction over the endpoint gap proves exactness of the recursion.  At a nonsingular allowed coordinate, every solution of the system before substitution must have the value (8), and every solution of the substituted system lifts uniquely by (8).  At a singular or forbidden coordinate, no variable or equation needed for compatibility is discarded.  After the finitely many pairs have been processed, all transition equations not used for an equivalent substitution, all covariance equations (2), and all strict inequalities (3) remain imposed after the accumulated substitutions.  Therefore, if \(\mathfrak R_b\) denotes the residual semialgebraic realization on diagonal branch \(b\), reconstruction gives
\[
 \mathcal S(B,Q;G)
   =\bigcup_b \operatorname{Rec}_b(\mathfrak R_b),                 \tag{10}
\]
where equality is literal, rather than equality only after topological or Zariski closure.

Each \(\mathfrak R_b\) is a finite Boolean combination of polynomial equalities and strict polynomial inequalities over \(K\).  There are finitely many branches and finitely many variables.  The cited lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}effective\mbox{-}cad\mbox{-}decision\mbox{-}sampling}\) therefore implies that CAD terminates on every branch, decides whether \(\mathfrak R_b\) is empty, and returns an exact represented point when it is nonempty.  By (10), all branch systems are empty if and only if \(\mathcal S(B,Q;G)=\varnothing\).  This proves termination, soundness, and completeness of the incompatibility output of \(\operatorname{Cert}_{uv,m,G}(B,Q)\).

It remains to prove that the other two outputs classify the transfer fiber exactly.  Suppose the compatible fiber is nonempty, and take two compatible points.  Write
\[
 p=A_{vu},\quad q=A_{vv},\qquad
 p'=A'_{vu},\quad q'=A'_{vv}.
\]
Stability gives \(|q|<1\) and \(|q'|<1\).  Hence, for every \(z\in\mathbb T\),
\[
 |qz|<1,\qquad |q'z|<1,
\]
so neither \(1-qz\) nor \(1-q'z\) vanishes; moreover \(z\neq0\).  Cross multiplication and cancellation of \(z\) are therefore valid, and the two transfers agree on \(\mathbb T\) if and only if
\[
 p(1-q'z)=p'(1-qz)\quad\text{for every }z\in\mathbb T.             \tag{11}
\]
The difference between the two sides of (11) is
\[
 (p-p')+(p'q-pq')z.                                                 \tag{12}
\]
Evaluating (12) at \(z=1\) and \(z=-1\) shows that it vanishes on \(\mathbb T\) if and only if both of its coefficients vanish.  Thus
\[
 h_{p,q}=h_{p',q'}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 p=p'\ \text{ and }\ pq'=p'q,                                     \tag{13}
\]
and, because all quantities are real,
\[
 h_{p,q}\neq h_{p',q'}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \Delta(p,q,p',q')
 :=(p-p')^2+(pq'-p'q)^2>0.                                         \tag{14}
\]
Equation (13) correctly identifies all pairs \((0,q)\) with the same zero transfer; equality of the coefficient pair itself is not required.

For each ordered pair of diagonal branches, take two copies of the corresponding complete residual systems and append the strict polynomial inequality (14), after reconstruction.  The finite union of these two-copy systems is feasible if and only if there exist two points of \(\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\) having unequal transfers, by (10), (14), \(\mathrm{def{:}pair\mbox{-}fiber}\), and \(\mathrm{def{:}transfer\mbox{-}fiber}\).  The cited CAD lemma decides this feasibility and, when it holds, supplies exact residual sample points.  Reconstruction produces attained pairs
\[
 (A,D),(A',D')\in\mathcal S(B,Q;G)
\]
satisfying
\[
 (A_{vu}-A'_{vu})^2+
 (A_{vu}A'_{vv}-A'_{vu}A_{vv})^2>0.
\]
Their strict diagonal and innovation inequalities are inherited from their branch systems, so the witnesses are stable and have positive diagonal innovation covariance.  This proves soundness of the ambiguity output, while the feasibility equivalence proves its completeness.

If every two-copy system is infeasible, (14) says that every two compatible points yield the same transfer.  A sample from any nonempty one-copy branch then supplies \((p,q)\) and hence the common exact rational function
\[
 z\longmapsto\frac{pz}{1-qz}.
\]
Conversely, if \(\mathcal H_{uv}(B,Q;G)\) is a singleton, no two-copy system can satisfy (14), so the certificate returns this common function.  This establishes both directions of the singleton assertion and, together with the incompatibility and ambiguity cases, proves the claimed trichotomy for the algorithm in \(\mathrm{def{:}certificate}\).

All advertised exceptional cases are included in these equivalences.  Zero diagonal roots are retained in (5) and are sent to the singular residual system whenever the divided difference vanishes.  A forbidden queried edge, or an allowed queried edge forced to zero by compatibility, is handled by (13).  Open and positive-dimensional fibers are handled directly by the cited CAD lemma with the strict inequalities (3).  Branch duplication or merger cannot affect the answer because (10) is a union and the two-copy test ranges over every ordered branch pair.  No rank, overlap, conditioning, boundary relaxation, or limiting premise is used, and no division is made without the explicit nonzero condition in (8).

For completeness, the first requested exact stress test is realized inside the encoded fiber.  Let \(d=2\), \(m=3\), let \(G\) contain \(1\to2\), and set \(B=0\) and \(Q=I_2\).  Define
\[
 A_{\pm}=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\ \pm\tfrac12&0\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 D_{\pm}=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(1,\tfrac34\right).
\]
Then \(A_{\pm}^2=0\), and hence
\[
 A_{\pm}^3=0=B,
 \qquad
 \sum_{r=0}^{2}A_{\pm}^rD_{\pm}(A_{\pm}^r)^\top
 =D_{\pm}+A_{\pm}D_{\pm}A_{\pm}^\top
 =\operatorname{diag}\!\left(1,\tfrac34\right)
  +\operatorname{diag}\!\left(0,\tfrac14\right)
 =I_2.
\]
Both points satisfy \(\rho(A_{\pm})=0<1\) and \(D_{\pm}\succ0\), while their transfers are \(z/2\) and \(-z/2\).  Thus the two-copy system contains stable, strictly positive, transfer-distinct witnesses rather than only boundary points, so exact CAD cannot return a singleton in this case.

For the second stress test, let \(d=2\), \(m=2\), and let \((A,D)\) be any compatible point with \(A_{21}\neq0\).  The support zeros and lower-triangular form are preserved by \(A\mapsto-A\), as are stability and positivity of \(D\), and
\[
 (-A)^2=A^2,
 \qquad
 D+(-A)D(-A)^\top=D+ADA^\top.
\]
Thus \((-A,D)\) is a second compatible point for the same \((B,Q)\).  With \(p=A_{21}\), \(q=A_{22}\), \(p'=-p\), and \(q'=-q\),
\[
 \Delta(p,q,-p,-q)
 =(2p)^2+\{p(-q)-(-p)q\}^2
 =4p^2>0.
\]
Hence every nonzero-edge two-variable \(m=2\) case retains the global sign pair, as required.
